messages.content: What kind of fertilizer is best for growing tomatoes?

function.name: soil_analysis_analyze_soil_type
function.description: Analyze a type of soil and provides characteristics about it. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

soil_type.description: The type of the soil. For example, loam, sandy, etc.

parameters_needed.description: Optional specific characteristics of the soil to analyze.

message.content: For tomatoes, a balanced fertilizer with a higher middle number (nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium) is usually best. A common recommendation is a 5-10-10 or 6-12-12 blend, which supplies enough phosphorus for root development and potassium for fruit quality while keeping nitrogen moderate to avoid excessive leafy growth. If you prefer organic options, a composted manure or a fish emulsion can work well, especially if your soil already has good organic matter. Always consider doing a soil test first to tailor the exact NPK ratio to your soil’s needs.
